content: Tylenol PM is a proprietary medication that combines acetaminophen (paracetamol) and diphenhydramine, manufactured and distributed by Johnson & Johnson. It is specifically formulated as both an analgesic and a sedative, meaning it is designed to relieve pain and promote sleep. This medication is commonly used to address occasional headaches and minor aches or pains that are accompanied by difficulty sleeping. It is classified as non-habit forming. Acetaminophen, one of the active ingredients, is also sold independently under the brand name Tylenol. Diphenhydramine, the other active ingredient, is marketed separately as Simply Sleep and is also the primary component in Benadryl, which is used to treat allergies. Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine, and in addition to its use in allergy relief, it is also found in Benylin, where it serves as an antitussive (anti-cough agent) in cough and cold treatments. The sedative or drowsy effect associated with Tylenol PM is primarily due to the antihistaminic properties of diphenhydramine. Tylenol PM has also been implicated in the production of a street drug known as Cheese, which is a combination of Tylenol PM and black tar heroin. This drug has gained popularity among teenagers, particularly in the Dallas, Texas area. In response to this issue, some retail stores in the Dallas region have removed Tylenol PM from their shelves. This decision was made because store managers suspected that individuals involved in the production of Cheese were shoplifting Tylenol PM to obtain its ingredients.
